title: Research
text: Our themes follow the chain from physics to behavior: model the vehicle, estimate its state, control it, and sense the water around it.

title: Research
text:
Dynamic modelling and control
Nonlinear six-degree-of-freedom models of our vehicles, built on standard marine-craft formulations, and controllers designed from them. Marjan-R1 has a derived model and open-loop pool validation. Closed-loop control is the next step.
Platforms: Marjan-R1

title: Research
text:
State estimation and system identification
Fusing inertial, pressure and sonar data, and fitting model parameters from experiments. Marjan-R1 is instrumented for system identification.
[TO CONFIRM: current status of this work.]

title: Research
text:
Energy-aware autonomy
Deciding when to act, not only how, to extend battery life. Our event-triggered glider control reduces energy use in simulation.

title: Marjan-R1 ROV
text:
Integrated prototype. Validated in controlled pool experiments.
Marjan-R1 is an inspection-class remotely operated vehicle designed and built in-house: frame, pressure housings, electronics, firmware and control software. It is a research platform, so we can change any layer of it.

title: Marjan-R1 ROV
text:
Design notes

Neutrally buoyant open frame in HDPE with closed-cell foam floats. The center of gravity sits below the center of buoyancy, which gives passive stability.
Eight thrusters at the frame corners, angled to give six-degree-of-freedom control. A thruster allocation matrix maps commanded forces and moments to thruster inputs.
Modular electronics stack with over-the-air firmware updates.
Sensors: inertial measurement unit, pressure sensor for depth, and ping sonar. The architecture allows a Doppler velocity log later.

title: KFUPM Marine Robotics Lab
text:
Problems we address
Underwater structures and water bodies are hard to observe, and periodic surveys leave gaps between observations. We work on:



Submerged infrastructure


Inspecting piers, berths, walls and intakes without sending divers into the water.




Ports, marinas and engineered waterways


Condition records over time instead of occasional snapshots.




Coastal and environmental monitoring


Water-quality sensing is a target application. It is not yet integrated on any of our platforms.

title: KFUPM Marine Robotics Lab
text:
Featured result


[FIGURE PLACEHOLDER: open-loop step responses, Marjan-R1 (own plot)]


A dynamic model of a compact six-degree-of-freedom ROV
We derived a nonlinear model of Marjan-R1 and compared it with open-loop step responses from pool tests. The tests confirmed static buoyancy trim and showed strong coupling between axes, which is why we are developing closed-loop control. See the publications.

title: Applications & Partnerships
text: Many underwater assets and water bodies are checked by periodic dive campaigns or vessel surveys. Those leave gaps between observations. We are building the vehicles, models and sensing needed to close those gaps, and we want to test them against real operating problems.

title: Applications & Partnerships
text:
Problems we work on



Submerged infrastructure inspection


Piers, berths, canal walls, revetments and intake structures need assessment below the surface. Robotic inspection can document their condition and reduce the need for divers to enter the water.




Ports and marinas


Regular condition records of berths and basins.




Engineered waterways and water bodies


Enclosed basins, lagoons and canals where conditions change over time, and trends matter more than a single survey.




Coastal and environmental monitoring


Repeated observation of coastal water. Water-quality sensing is a target application. It is not yet integrated on any of our platforms, and no autonomous monitoring has been demonstrated.




Sensor and autonomy validation


A controlled setting to test sensors, estimators and control software on a real vehicle before field use.

title: Applications & Partnerships
text:
Why work with us

We own the whole stack. Mechanical design, electronics, firmware, models and control software are ours, so the vehicle can be changed to suit the problem. Marjan-R1 is not a modified commercial platform.
Model-based development. Each vehicle comes with a dynamic model and simulation, so behavior is tested before it is tried in water.
Open about status. We tell you what has been demonstrated and where, and what has not.
A university lab with a path to product. We do academic research and intend to commercialize our underwater robotics capability, eventually through a spin-off. [TO CONFIRM wording]

title: Underwater glider
text:
Modeled and simulated. Hardware in development.
Underwater gliders change their buoyancy to dive and climb, and shift an internal mass to control pitch, so they use little energy. We study how to make them last longer on a battery.

title: Underwater glider
section: What we have shown, in simulation
text:
What we have shown, in simulation
An energy-aware, event-triggered geometric controller formulated on the special Euclidean group SE(3). In simulation on a Seawing-class glider model, it used more than 45% less energy and 31% fewer control updates than a conventional time-triggered controller over the same mission, with a modest increase in tracking error.
